flow: browser count mode -> partition-by-partition hosted verification -> merged occurrences -> honest partial-scan reporting

semantics.partitions: the recording's registered windows, in source order
semantics.verification: the existing visual source check (eight sampled frames) per partition, zero extra context
semantics.merge_rule: verified occurrences whose spans overlap within half a second become one event; each event keeps every supporting verification ID
semantics.budget: max_checks (default 60, at most 500) bounds hosted checks; exhausted scans report partial counts
semantics.uncertain: insufficient_evidence partitions are counted and reported, never treated as absence
semantics.date_scope: the same capture-date scoping as search; undated recordings are skipped and reported

real_browser_run.query: the robot arm moves a cup
real_browser_run.merge_behavior: the same cup action was reported by two adjacent overlapping windows and merged into one event
real_browser_run.note_shown: The count covers only checked partitions; unchecked or uncertain intervals are not proven absent, and nearby separate events can merge into one occurrence.

tests.count_suite: 6 passed ungated against a labelled local VLM fixture (validation, merge, separate events, partial budget, uncertain partitions, date-scope skip)

limits: A count is an observed count over checked partitions, never proof of the true total; partial scans say so.
Occurrences within half a second merge into one event; two distinct events closer than that cannot be separated by this rule.
Sparse eight-frame sampling can miss brief actions inside a checked partition.
Long recordings need many hosted checks; the budget stops scans and reports what remains.
One 22-second demo; not a counting-accuracy benchmark.
